title: The periodic tensor calculation for a square-zero exact divisor
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $t\in R$ satisfy $t^2=0$ and $\{r\in R:tr=0\}=tR$. Put $F=R/tR$. The augmented sequence $\cdots\xrightarrow{t}R\xrightarrow{t}R\to F\to0$ is a free resolution, and for every $q\geq0$ one has $H^{-q}(F\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}F)\cong F$, equivalently $\operatorname{Tor}^R_q(F,F)\cong F$. Here derived tensor is computed from K-flat resolutions [def-pc-kflat-complex] in the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For every scheme $V$, let $R_V,F_V$ denote constant sheaves on $V_{\mathrm{proét}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Then $H^{-q}(F_V\otimes_{R_V}^{\mathbf L}F_V)\cong F_V$ for every $q\geq0$, with derived tensor as in [def-weil-derived-tensor]. If $F\ne0$ and $V$ is nonempty, all these sheaves are nonzero.

source.place: The examples, periodic multiplication resolution; generalized from Z/ell^2 to an exact square-zero divisor

proof.text: Construct the nonnegative chain complex with R in every degree and multiplication by t as differential. The equation t^2=0 makes its differential square zero. The annihilator hypothesis identifies every positive-degree kernel with the image of the preceding differential. The quotient augmentation is surjective and has kernel (t). This gives the concrete Mathlib ProjectiveResolution, with the identity identifications of its free terms.

source.place: The examples: the periodic multiplication resolution, with t in place of ell

proof.text: Use ProjectiveResolution.isoLeftDerivedObj to compute Tor from this resolution. Tensoring the multiplication differential with R/(t) gives zero, by the balanced tensor relations. Extend the projective resolution by zero to a cochain complex. Its terms are projective and hence flat, and it is bounded above. Apply the proved source-library K-flat criterion and DerivedCategory.QObjTensorSingleFunctorObjIso to compute the monoidal derived self-tensor. In both calculations isoHomologyπ and iCyclesIso identify homology of the zero-differential tensor complex with its term. Unit tensor isomorphisms identify that term with R/(t), including degree zero.

source.place: Tag 064K, lemma-derived-tor-quasi-isomorphism; computation following the periodic resolution in the blueprint

proof.text: For the pro-etale site lift the coefficient ring and quotient module to the universe max(r,u+1). The lifted quotient ring map is surjective with kernel generated by the lifted t; the linear first-isomorphism theorem identifies its quotient with the lifted original quotient. Form the constant module presheaf functor, then sheafify along the commutative-ring sheafification unit. Evaluation identifies the constant presheaf functor with the identity, so it preserves finite limits and colimits; exact module sheafification preserves these properties. Its canonical maps to the unit and to the restricted unit of the constant quotient ring are isomorphisms, because their underlying maps are locally bijective sheafification units. Thus this functor carries the scalar periodic resolution to a resolution of precisely the canonical squareZeroQuotientModule.

source.place: Tag 093J, lemma-constant-exact; constant sheaves of modules in section-constant

proof.text: Each nonpositive term of the sheafified resolution is isomorphic to the tensor unit and each positive term is zero. The tensor unit is flat because tensoring by it is isomorphic to the identity functor; zero objects are flat because tensoring by them is zero. Transfer categorical flatness through siteSheafTensorRightIso. Apply the already proved independent-coefficient bounded-above flat criterion, which does not equate coefficient and site universes.

source.place: Tag 06YQ, lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat, and section-flat derived tensor construction

proof.text: Compare the intrinsic tensor construction with any K-flat first-factor model. An isomorphism in the derived category admits a common roof of quasi-isomorphisms by DerivedCategory.right_fac. Choose such roofs for the two factor comparisons and resolve the middle object of the second roof by a K-flat complex. Tensoring each roof leg with a K-flat second factor preserves quasi-isomorphisms; alternate these localized isomorphisms with the Koszul braiding to obtain an isomorphism between the tensor models. Apply this to the representatives and K-flat resolution actually chosen by ringedSiteDerivedTensorOfUniverses and the explicit sheafified periodic resolution.

source.place: Tag 06YQ, lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat, and section-flat derived tensor construction

proof.text: Naturality of the sheafification adjunction identifies the sheafified scalar differential with multiplication by the constant section t on the unit. Before sheafification, the balanced tensor relations move this scalar to the quotient factor, where it is zero. Naturality of the proved tensorRightPresentation identifies the sheaf tensor map with sheafification of this zero presheaf map, so the sheaf tensor differential is zero. The source-library single-factor total-tensor isomorphism identifies tensor with F[0] with termwise tensor by F. Compute its homology by isoHomologyπ and iCyclesIso and identify its negative-degree term with F using the unit isomorphism. This gives H^(-q)=F for every nonnegative q.

source.place: Tag 06YQ, lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat, and section-flat derived tensor construction

proof.text: At a nonempty pro-etale object the constant commutative-ring sheafification unit is injective: an equality of two distinct constant sections would make the bottom equalizer sieve covering. Push this covering along the continuous forgetful functor to schemes. The pro-etale topology is below the jointly surjective topology, so the bottom sieve cannot cover a nonempty scheme. Evaluate a hypothetically zero canonical quotient module at the identity pro-etale object over V. Its underlying quotient-ring sections would be subsingleton, making the images of 1 and 0 equal. Injectivity contradicts the nontriviality of the scalar quotient. The displayed cohomology isomorphisms then give all asserted nonvanishings.
